title: Terminator-aware JSON append protocol and client guidance for streaming structured output
creator: Priya Patel
description: Problem statement: When delivering structured JSON via streaming endpoints (SSE/websocket/chunked HTTP) we observe multiple failure modes: mid-token truncation, UTF-8 boundary splits, LLM-inserted ellipses or explanatory trailing text, and accidental inclusion of bytes that collide with simple sentinels. These failures are particularly painful when combined with function/tool-calling: tool payloads are emitted before the server or client can reliably determine the object boundary, causing duplicate tool invocations or dropped state. This ticket defines a lightweight, terminator-aware append protocol plus client guidance to ensure safe truncation handling, idempotent resumes, and unambiguous tool-call semantics.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a streaming chat generation where model is producing a JSON object with nested arrays and a function_call block.
2) Simulate network interruption mid-chunk so the final chunk contains a partial Unicode codepoint and an incomplete JSON object (e.g., ends at '\"actions\": [ {\"type\": \"open', no closing braces).
3) Client retries by re-requesting the same response without an explicit resume token; the service replays last N tokens which overlap leading to duplicate tool invocation on the consumer side.
4) Observe parsing failures or double-executed tools in the consumer pipeline (race between parse success and tool dispatch).
proposed_solution: Introduce a small, backward-compatible stream envelope and client guidance: 1) Envelope metadata chunk: the first chunk for each logical response MUST include an 'envelope' JSON line specifying: format (ndjson|json-stream), seq_start (int), terminator (an opaque hex string or chosen sentinel), object_id (UUID) and checksum_algo (e.g., sha256). 2) Terminator semantics: the server may append an explicit terminator chunk (a single line equal to the terminator token) to mark finality. Terminator must be chosen per-response and is escaped in payloads by prepending an escape byte sequence (e.g., 0x1B) when found. 3) Sequence numbers: every chunk after the envelope includes seq (monotonic int) and payload (string). Client can detect missing seq and request resume_from_seq. 4) Resume and backfill policy: on interruption client issues a resume request referencing object_id and highest-seen seq. Server either replays from resume_from_seq or sends a backfill chunk with backfill=true and a backfill_from_seq header that fills the gap. 5) Idempotent tool-calls: tool call events MUST be emitted as separate top-level ndjson objects with stable call_id and call_seq; client should only dispatch a tool if call_id has not been executed locally. 6) Truncation repair: if server cannot replay full object it must emit a 'truncation_hint' with token_boundary (token id or byte offset) and a recommended repair mode: 'retry-llm-complete' (server re-runs continuation with deterministic settings) or 'consumer-recompose' (client concatenates last valid fragment and requests a short completion call). 7) Fallback: when terminator is not present after a configurable timeout, server will publish a 'graceful_end' with reason = partial|failed and a partial_checksum that lets clients decide whether to treat result as final. 8) Backwards compatibility: if client does not send resume requests, server behaves as today for simple streaming but includes envelope if supported. 9) Sample server/client snippets and libraries will be added to SDKs and the Console docs.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime and sdk teams.
Server emits envelope metadata chunk for new streaming responses behind a feature flag.
Client SDK (node/python) can resume with resume_from_seq semantics and avoid double tool dispatch using call_id dedup table.
Automated integration tests simulate mid-chunk truncation and verify no duplicate tool executions and successful reconstruction or clear graceful_end semantics.
Perf impact under normal (non-interrupted) streaming is <3% p50 latency increase when envelope flag is enabled.
Migration plan documented: how to opt-in customers and toggle flag for Dedicated/Private deployments.
notes: Design tradeoffs considered: length-prefixing every object (robust but high overhead) vs. per-response terminator (lightweight, acceptable tradeoffs for real-time).

Escape strategy: we prefer an 8-byte opaque hex terminator chosen by server to minimize collisions rather than a well-known sequence. Escaping payloads is required when the terminator occurs naturally.
Tokenizer-aware truncation: the runtime can expose token id offsets in truncation_hint to help deterministic re-completion. This ties into the kernel/runtime mapping work (see dependency).
comments: Priya Patel (2026-03-11): initial draft — proposing per-response terminator to reduce protocol overhead vs full length-prefixing.
Emma Liu (2026-03-12): +1 on call_id deduping; we should add guidance for server-side dedupe as well for multi-replica environments.
Mateo Alvarez (2026-03-13): Concern: escaping adds CPU for large payloads. Suggest heuristic: only escape if terminator occurs, otherwise no extra pass.
